newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on ample liquidity.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 40 basis points at 28.60 percent on Wednesday due to an easing in liquidity objectives, traders said.

"Trading was much more relaxed than for many recent sessions. Paper was on offer, despite month-end demand for liquidity and banks having to settle outstanding accounts with the central bank today," said a dealer.
Overnight rates did reach an earlier high of 29.70 percent, but fell to a low of 28.50 percent.
"Banco de Mexico's change in its liquidity objective is still having an effect," the dealer added.
The central bank announced on Tuesday it had changed its liquidity object to zero, from minus 20 million pesos, which had been in force since October 14.
Traders said a relatively stable peso and across-the-board falls in primary rates at Tuesday night's auction also helped overnight rates to fall.
Analysts forecast little additional upside pressure on yields for the remainder of the year.
"Demand for paper is still healthy. Demand was up at the auction from last week, which shows that investors are still interested in debt positions," said a trader.
Banco de Mexico earlier injected 5.046 billion pesos into the market by auctioning four credits, which it assigned at between 30.28 and 30.53 percent.

Credit maturities for Thursday were expected to total 3.608 billion pesos, although traders pointed out that the ensuing liquidity shortage would be eased by an underplacement of 148 million pesos carried over from Tuesday's primary auction.
